title: Fix elapsed days calculation to ignore time component
prompt: The function days_between(d1, d2) in starter/date_diff.py accepts two ISO-8601 date strings (YYYY-MM-DD) and returns the absolute number of days between them as an integer. The current implementation includes an off-by-one error caused by using datetime instead of date, and it fails when dates are passed in reverse order. Fix it so that days_between('2024-01-01', '2024-01-10') == 9, days_between('2024-01-10', '2024-01-01') == 9 (absolute), days_between('2023-12-31', '2024-01-01') == 1, and days_between('2024-02-28', '2024-03-01') == 2. Do not edit the tests.

starter_files.date_diff.py:
from datetime import datetime


def days_between(d1, d2):
    """Return the number of days between two ISO date strings."""
    dt1 = datetime.fromisoformat(d1)
    dt2 = datetime.fromisoformat(d2)
    return (dt2 - dt1).days
